newsitem.title: UK: British Labour would win 41-seat majority-pollster.
newsitem.headline: British Labour would win 41-seat majority-pollster.

text.p: Bob Worcester, chairman of polling organisation MORI, predicted on Thursday that the British election would take place on May 1 and Labour would emerge with an overall majority of 41 seats.
The election must be held by May 22, with May 1 widely considered the favourite date of Prime Minister John Major.
Worcester, Britain's best known pollster, predicted at a conference that Labour would win 350 seats against 246, or perhaps 250, for the ruling Conservatives.
But he told reporters that Labour would have only 41 percent of the vote against 35 percent for the Conservatives: a lead that is well below the 20-point gap shown in recent polls.
Worcester explained this by saying many "natural Tories (Conservatives)" whose main aim was to get rid of Major would vote for the centrist Liberal Democarats rather than for Labour.
The Liberal Democrats would get 21 percent of the vote and 36 seats, he said. Other parties would get a combined 27 seats.
Worcester said polls showed 60 percent of voters felt health was important in their choice of party, while 51 percent cited education, 48 percent unemployment and 45 percent law and order.
Labour was felt to have the best policies on the first three issues and the Conservatives ranked top on law and order, but only by a small margin.
Europe was important in the choice of party for only 19 percent of voters and taxation for just 26 percent.
